column2: Read this as a bubbly, sparkling, warm South African English primary school teacher who is delighted to see the child: big smile in the voice, lively and playful, full of wonder and encouragement, but still clear and unhurried for a 5-year-old. Natural South African English accent. Leave a short pause between the lines.
column3: Hello! This is Bip, a little robot who loves sounds. Click on an island to start exploring! ... Welcome to Numbers Island! Click Bip, and let's count. ... Find the picture that starts with... ... Drag the letters to build the word in the picture. ... Wow! You really know that sound now! ... Nearly! Have another listen. ... Bip's battery is low, so he's having a rest. When the battery is full, we can play again! ... Make a tower of seven blocks. ... Three and two. How many altogether?

column2: Lees dit as 'n bruisende, sprankelende, warm Suid-Afrikaanse graad R-juffrou wat verheug is om die kind te sien: 'n groot glimlag in die stem, lewendig en speels, vol verwondering en aanmoediging, maar steeds duidelik en rustig vir 'n vyfjarige. Natuurlike Afrikaanse uitspraak. Laat 'n kort pouse tussen die reëls.
column3: Hallo! Dit is Bip, 'n klein robot wat baie lief is vir klanke. Klik op 'n eiland om te begin! ... Welkom op Getalle-eiland! Klik op Bip, dan tel ons saam. ... Drie en twee. Hoeveel is dit altesaam? ... Bou 'n toring van sewe blokke. ... Goed gedoen! Jy het dit reg gekry. ... Amper! Luister nog 'n keer. ... Bip se battery is pap, so hy rus 'n bietjie. Wanneer die battery vol is, kan ons weer speel!
